title: Sharry: An Efficient and Sharing Far Memory System
problem: Existing Far Memory Systems cannot efficiently handle large loads and have low memory utilization, preventing multiple processes from sharing memory nodes and limiting FMS scalability to multi-tenant scenarios.
motivation: Far memory systems extend system memory capacity, but poor sharing capabilities prevent their practical deployment in multi-process environments where multiple applications need to share remote memory nodes.
method: Sharry puts all processes into one shared memory address space, eliminating the expensive overhead of switching between separate memory views. It carefully manages far memory (memory stored elsewhere) by dividing it into small chunks and moving them around to keep storage utilization high. It also assigns memory blocks using dedicated CPU cores, allowing multiple processes to share memory without slowing down the main processors.
key_novelty: Instead of isolating each process's memory separately, Sharry lets multiple processes share a single far memory system by putting them in one unified address space.
contributions: Unified address space design for multi-process far memory sharing
Fine-grained memory management for improved utilization
Dedicated CPU core allocation strategy for load handling
45% memory utilization improvement with 9% performance overhead in sharing scenarios
limitations: Evaluation limited to single memory node sharing; scalability to multiple nodes not discussed.
